executionSurface: isolated candidate Router, locked candidate Switchyard, native Codex app-server parent and one explicit synthetic child role
classifierInput: Each new assignment reached the authenticated Switchyard hop as its exact current plaintext projection; tool continuations carried no projection.
firstRequestGate: The first actual named child used the temporary provider and switchyard/auto role before later turns ran.
failureTransitionTest: An integrated Rust server test retains a non-default target for a tool continuation, then consumes a null new-assignment projection marker, releases affinity, selects Sol Medium and leaves the Jev call count unchanged.
nativeCompatibilityFinding: Responses Lite requires synthesized relay calls to set reasoning.context=all_turns and parallel_tool_calls=false; the candidate now does so and has focused Router coverage.
limitations: This is isolated predeployment evidence and cannot certify or promote the installed runtime to v2.
The run used four fresh synthetic assignments and one child; it is bounded evidence rather than a statistical reliability guarantee.

G1 observed projection latency and native relay token cost on its six-case corpus; the code enforces a 5-second projection wait, but neither G1 nor this isolated run guarantees a token bound or future latency distribution.
The native relay is model-generated extraction, not a documented decrypt API.
